calls.reason: The packet contains neither Nestler’s original proof nor an independent review of it. The benchmark’s other failures cannot establish that this particular proof was invalid.
Petrov et al.’s original evaluation reports that all tested models consistently claimed success despite defective proofs. That directly supports Marcus’s description of their submitted answers.

The Nature study found explanations inflated users’ confidence. Microsoft researchers observed trust in fabricated citations, even resistance when errors were identified, supporting the ordinary claim of easy uncritical trust.
The prompting studies show mixed abstention results on multiple-choice tasks, not recognition of failed proofs. They also cannot establish what evidence the authors had personally seen.

The AlphaProof paper establishes Lean verification, but the packet leaves AlphaGeometry 2’s guarantee unresolved. The documented proof gap concerns its predecessor, making the evidence mixed for the cited systems.

Tow Center found substantial article-retrieval errors, while YouGov found divided trust. Neither establishes the claimed mismatch between non-specialist users’ expectations and reliability across ordinary questions.
